question: An article is marked at ₹1,500 and sold for ₹1,200. Find the percentage discount.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = MP − SP = 1500 − 1200 = ₹300

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

Discount % = (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

Discount % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Discount
 ₹300

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,500

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,200

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 1500 − 1200

⇒ Discount = ₹300

⇒ Discount % = (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by: Effective Discount = (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Markup Price

It is the price written on the article to show a higher value before applying a discount. MP = CP + Markup Amount.
